title: Sadhguru Calls Mount Kailash the 'Greatest Mystical Library on the Planet' During Historic Motorbike Yatra
excerpt: The Isha Foundation founder made the remark to actor R. Madhavan during his 17-day Kailash journey — undertaken on a motorbike after recovering from two brain surgeries.
body:
• Sadhguru described Mount Kailash as 'the greatest mystical library on the planet and in the known universe' during a conversation with actor R. Madhavan on his recent Kailash Yatra
  • The spiritual leader completed the 17-day journey on a motorbike — a historic first — after recovering from two major brain surgeries
  • The Kailash Yatra route through Tibet reopened after a five-year hiatus, reflecting improving India-China relations
  • In yogic tradition, Kailash is considered a repository where great sages from multiple traditions have 'deposited' their spiritual knowledge over millennia

Sadhguru, the founder of the Isha Foundation, described Mount Kailash as "the greatest mystical library on the planet and in the known universe" during his recent Kailash Yatra — a 17-day pilgrimage he undertook on a motorbike in what was described as a historic first.

The remark, made during a conversation with actor R. Madhavan while en route to the sacred peak, has drawn renewed attention to the spiritual significance of Kailash across Hindu, Buddhist, Jain, and Bon traditions.

A Journey of Recovery and Resilience

Sadhguru's motorbike pilgrimage was remarkable not just for its mode of travel but for the context. The 69-year-old spiritual leader undertook the journey after recovering from two major brain surgeries, crediting yoga for his physical endurance. He reportedly promised his doctors: "No jerks, no bumps, no falls."

To prepare, Sadhguru completed a Trans-Canada motorcycle ride to test his readiness for the demanding Himalayan terrain. Along the way, he was joined by actors Kangana Ranaut and R. Madhavan, cricketer Varun Chakravarthy, and filmmaker Nag Ashwin, sharing insights on spirituality, recovery, and the significance of the journey.

What Does 'Mystical Library' Mean?

Sadhguru has long described Kailash not as a place of information but of transformation. In yogic cosmology, the mountain — also known as Meru — is considered the axis upon which all existence revolves, a bridge between the physical and metaphysical worlds.

"Starting from Shiva himself, many great beings chose to deposit and preserve their work in Kailash. Rishabadev, the saints of the Bon religion, two of the greatest Buddhist teachers, Agastyamuni, the Nayanmars — all of them chose Kailash Parvat."

— Sadhguru

According to Sadhguru, the impressions and spiritual knowledge of thousands of yogis are embedded in the mountain's energy field. Unlike a conventional library, this is not a repository that can be read — it must be experienced. "It is not a place of information; it is a place of transformation," he has said.

The mountain holds significance across four major spiritual traditions. Hindus consider it the abode of Lord Shiva and Goddess Parvati. Buddhists regard it as the home of Buddha Demchok. Jains believe the first Tirthankara, Rishabhadeva, attained spiritual liberation there. The Tibetan Bon tradition considers it the seat of all spiritual power.

Kailash Route Reopens After Five Years

The Yatra was made possible by the reopening of the Kailash pilgrimage route through Tibet after a five-year closure, a development seen as reflecting the gradual improvement in India-China relations. The route had been closed since 2020 due to COVID-19 restrictions and bilateral tensions.

For the Indian diaspora, the reopening of the Kailash route holds particular significance. The pilgrimage has long been considered one of the most transformative spiritual journeys in Hindu and Buddhist traditions, and the five-year disruption affected thousands of devotees who had planned the trek.

During a conversation with Kangana Ranaut, who asked about Shiva, Sadhguru replied: "I sit on his shoulders, so everything is fine" — a characteristically enigmatic response that emphasized experiential spirituality over intellectual understanding.
